description: Provision/undo a git worktree's gitignored local state from the primary checkout, driven by project config (#532)

worktree.description: A fresh `git worktree add` never brings gitignored local state along — vendored binaries, machine-specific DB config, a generated asset cache — so a project's test suite fails there in whatever misleading way each missing piece produces (OOM, an empty exception, a wrong-looking red). `worktree:setup[:PATH]` (PATH defaults to cwd) provisions PATH from the repo's primary checkout using `ops.worktree.setup` in `.supertool.json` — nothing project-specific lives in this op itself. Three configured lists: `link` (symlinked — for large, immutable, shared artefacts only; a write through a symlink is a write to the primary checkout), `copy` (copied, never linked — for anything machine-specific or that the worktree might mutate; `shutil.copytree(..., symlinks=False)`/`copy2`, never `os.symlink`, under any code path), `exclude` (appended to a worktree-PRIVATE exclude file, so a symlinked artefact can never be swept into a commit by `git add -A`/`git add .` — NOT `.git/info/exclude`, which git shares across every worktree of a repo; this uses `extensions.worktreeConfig` + a private `core.excludesFile` instead). No config declared is a clean no-op naming where to declare one, never an error and never a guess. Every entry reports one of three outcomes — linked/copied/excluded, already-there (idempotent re-run), or a WARNING (never a failure) for a source missing from the primary checkout, since some artefacts are legitimately regenerated on demand. A path declared in both `link` and `copy` is refused under both headings rather than guessed. `worktree:teardown[:PATH]` undoes exactly what `setup` recorded creating (a manifest written to the worktree's own private git dir, `.git/worktrees/<name>/worktree-setup/manifest.json` — never the working tree, so it cannot be committed by accident either) and leaves everything else — including a real file the user happens to have at the same path — untouched. PATH is deliberately exempt from the generic cwd/repo path-containment gate (\"paths\": {\"args\": []}) because pointing outside cwd IS the use case — provisioning a sibling worktree, or reading the primary checkout from inside a linked one. In its place, the op enforces its own boundary: PATH must resolve to a worktree of the SAME repository this call was invoked from, or it is refused by name before anything runs. See docs/presets/worktree.md.
